firmware.title: Bluetooth Firmware Selection
firmware.manual_instructions:
1. Click 'Open Download Page' to open kernel.org
2. Download the fw and config files
3. Click 'Open Config Folder' and place the files there
firmware.vendor_intel: Intel adapter (experimental): no Realtek files needed. If it starts in bootloader mode, place the matching ibt-*.sfi and ibt-*.ddc files from linux-firmware (intel/) in the config folder. AX210 and newer are not supported yet.
firmware.vendor_broadcom: Broadcom adapter (experimental): no Realtek files needed. It runs on its ROM firmware; optionally place a PatchRAM file such as BCM20702A1-0b05-17cb.hcd in the config folder.
firmware.vendor_csr: CSR adapter: no firmware files needed.
firmware.vendor_unsupported: This adapter needs a firmware loader that A2DPWB does not have (MediaTek / Qualcomm). It may not work.

settings.title: Settings...
settings.debug_mode_enabled:
Debug mode will take effect after you restart A2DPWB.

debug.log is then written to the config folder, and a Debug menu appears where you can start and stop an HCI packet capture (up to about 0.5 GB per hour while streaming).
settings.debug_mode_disabled:
Debug mode will be turned off after you restart A2DPWB.

Existing debug.log and HCI capture (.pklg) files stay in the config folder until you delete them.
advanced.max_packet_help:
Upper limit for the audio data in each Bluetooth packet (%d-%d). The headphones' own limit (MTU) always applies too; A2DPWB uses the smaller of the two.

%d (recommended) fits one Bluetooth baseband packet. Larger values save only 1-2%% overhead, but more audio is lost when a packet is lost. Applies from the next connection.

quality.title: Link Quality
quality.not_streaming: Not streaming. Values appear while audio is being sent.
quality.theory_value: %.0f kbps max, %.1f%% used (3-DH5 back to back)
quality.band_help: Packets occupy 1, 3 or 5 slots whatever their size, so radio time used is higher than the bandwidth share. Above about 80% little room is left for retransmissions and interference easily causes dropouts; lower the quality or turn on ABR in that case.
quality.loss_help: Packets are dropped before sending when the send queue is full (the radio cannot keep up) or L2CAP refuses them. Retransmissions over the air happen inside the Bluetooth controller and are not shown here.
